scenes.title: Leaving the wharf
scenes.caption: Handkerchiefs wave above the crowd as the frigate pulls away from Brooklyn. The little boats that follow her down the harbour turn back at the lightship. From there the Abraham Lincoln goes on alone.

scenes.title: The Horn from the frigate
scenes.caption: From the deck of the Abraham Lincoln, Cape Horn is a solitary rock fifteen miles to the north. The frigate turns northwest, and by the next day her screw is turning in Pacific water.

scenes.title: Rivets in the dark
scenes.caption: Aronnax runs a hand over the back that has carried the three men out of the water. Under his fingers are smooth plates joined by rivets. Ned stamps his foot, and the hollow hull rings.

scenes.title: The noon sight
scenes.caption: Nemo holds his sextant so still that Aronnax watches his hand. Below deck, the captain has clocks set to three different meridians. For his French guest he gives the reading from Paris.

scenes.title: Branches that spring back
scenes.caption: Every stem in the forest of Crespo grows straight up through the water. Aronnax pushes a branch aside to pass. As soon as he lets go, it stands upright again.

scenes.title: Fields below Mauna Kea
scenes.caption: From the platform Aronnax can pick out the cultivated strip along the coast of Hawaii. Behind the fields he sees one ridge after another, with the broad summit of Mauna Kea above them.

scenes.title: Blue fins and a golden tail
scenes.caption: Nuku Hiva stays on the horizon while the nets bring something of its waters aboard. Among the catch Aronnax picks out the dolphinfish by its blue fins and golden tail.

scenes.title: The wall below the reef
scenes.caption: Alongside the atoll, the electric lamps light up a wall that falls away for hundreds of metres. Conseil wants to know how long it took creatures so small to raise a reef so high.

scenes.title: Peaks to windward
scenes.caption: In the morning Aronnax can see Tahiti’s high peaks several miles to windward. The island slips astern, but mackerel and bonito from these waters find their way to the table aboard the Nautilus.

scenes.title: The papers in the tin
scenes.caption: Salt water has eaten into the box. Inside, La Pérouse’s sailing orders are still legible, down to the notes that Louis XVI wrote in the margins. Nemo lets Aronnax read them.

scenes.title: Breadfruit in the embers
scenes.caption: Ned cuts a breadfruit into thick slices and lays them on the embers. A thin crust forms around the soft white centre. After weeks of eating from the sea, the three men have something very like fresh bread.

scenes.title: Breakers on either side
scenes.caption: Beyond Cape Wessel the reefs stand farther apart. The charts give them in enough detail for the Nautilus to leave one line of breakers to port and the next reef to starboard.

scenes.title: A cross of coral
scenes.caption: A red coral cross rises from a heap of stones. The crew kneel around the new grave. When the men take their leave, each holds out a hand over the sand in a last farewell.

scenes.title: A shell for the collection
scenes.caption: Coconut palms mark the low shore as the crew haul in the nets. Aronnax sorts through the catch with Nemo’s collection in mind and sets aside a spiral shell.

scenes.title: Light on the water
scenes.caption: The stars are out, but the sea is brighter than the sky. Near midnight the bow slips back into dark water. Looking astern, Aronnax can still see the pale glow along the horizon.

scenes.title: A bag of oysters
scenes.caption: A stone on a rope carries the pearl fisher down from his boat. He fills the little bag at his waist with oysters, then kicks back to the surface for another breath. Nemo and his visitors watch from below.

scenes.title: Channels among the reefs
scenes.caption: Kiltan scarcely rises above its reef. With Ceylon astern, the course threads narrow channels between coral islands. From the surface the white water breaking along their rims is easier to see than the land.

scenes.title: Minarets on the headland
scenes.caption: For a moment Aronnax can distinguish the many-sided minarets of Aden against the bare hills. He expects Nemo to turn back here. By the following day they are on their way through Bab el Mandeb.

scenes.title: A muzzle above water
scenes.caption: From a distance the dugong looks asleep on the Red Sea. When it comes up for air, Aronnax can see the wide nostrils on top of its muzzle. Then its back slips under again.

scenes.title: Nemo at the wheel
scenes.caption: Aronnax stands beside Nemo in the pilot house. In the electric light he can see the rock walls stream past the glass. The roar of the current fills the little room.

scenes.title: The island below the waterline
scenes.caption: Aronnax knows Karpathos as the island where Proteus once tended his flocks in the old stories. His whole view of it from the saloon is a stretch of granite passing beyond the glass.

scenes.title: A hand at the glass
scenes.caption: The swimmer presses his face close to the saloon window. Aronnax thinks someone needs rescuing. Nemo makes a sign, the man answers with one hand, and the two part without a word.

scenes.title: An island in the making
scenes.caption: A current flows east from the Atlantic at the surface. Deeper in the strait another current runs west. It carries the Nautilus through the narrow passage and out into the open Atlantic.

scenes.title: The lower current
scenes.caption: Water from the Atlantic runs east at the surface. Down in the strait the flow reverses. The Nautilus rides that deeper current west, and within a few minutes the Mediterranean is astern.

scenes.title: Coins in the silt
scenes.caption: In the light outside the saloon Aronnax watches men stoop among the wrecked timbers. A chest has come apart on the bottom. The sailors gather its scattered coins, then go back for another load.

scenes.title: Streets by volcanic light
scenes.caption: Nemo leads Aronnax up a slope in the dark. From the crest the professor can trace streets between broken columns. The red light that reaches them comes from a volcano on the sea floor.

scenes.title: A patch of sky
scenes.caption: Aronnax climbs onto the platform expecting morning light. Far overhead he can make out a small patch of sky. The air he is breathing has come down through the mouth of the crater.

scenes.title: What the weed holds
scenes.caption: Small floats like berries keep the brown weed at the surface. Among its branches Aronnax can pick out bits of timber from lost ships. The Nautilus has room to travel beneath the tangle.

scenes.title: A camera in the saloon
scenes.caption: Aronnax wishes he could take home the sight of these bare rocks. Nemo has a camera brought to the window. The boat holds still while its electric lamps give the photographic plate enough light for an exposure.

scenes.title: Where the leads close
scenes.caption: For days the Nautilus has followed openings between the floes. Now the white blocks meet ahead of her. From the platform Aronnax can trace the edge of the pack as far as he can see in either direction.

scenes.title: The last of the sun
scenes.caption: At noon Nemo watches the rim of the sun touch the horizon. In the polar sea Verne imagined, this is the last sunset before six months of darkness. The black flag goes up on the rock.

scenes.title: Taking turns on the ice
scenes.caption: The men go out in shifts with air on their backs. Each time they return through the hatch, the air inside the Nautilus is a little harder to breathe. Outside, the cut in the ice is slowly deepening.

scenes.title: North by the Atlantic
scenes.caption: At seven in the evening the Nautilus is level with the Horn again. Aronnax has been following the mate’s pencil marks on the chart. Tonight he can tell Ned and Conseil that their course leads north into the Atlantic.

scenes.title: River water at sea
scenes.caption: A pale wash spreads from the river mouth into the darker Atlantic. It carries so much fresh water that the sea is less salty for leagues offshore.

scenes.title: An eye at the window
scenes.caption: Aronnax has been trying to describe a giant squid when one swims alongside. There is time to see the suckers on its arms and the colour of its eye. Then the propeller stops turning.

scenes.title: Sails in the Gulf Stream
scenes.caption: Schooners work along the coast and steamers pass on their way north. To Ned each sail off Cape Hatteras means someone might pick them up. The shore itself is still thirty miles away.

scenes.title: Stones among the shells
scenes.caption: Cod cruise over a bank strewn with pale shells. Among them lie boulders from farther north. Aronnax pictures the drifting ice that carried the stones out to sea and dropped them here.

scenes.title: A line across the seabed
scenes.caption: Conseil spots a long dark shape on the bottom and takes it for a sea serpent. It keeps its course as the Nautilus passes overhead. Aronnax tells him that messages travel along it between America and Europe.

scenes.title: A hull under white shells
scenes.caption: At first Aronnax sees only a pale mound. Beneath the crust of shells he begins to make out a hull with all its masts gone. Beside him, Nemo knows the ship well enough to tell its story from the day it was launched.

scenes.title: The notebook ashore
scenes.caption: In a fisherman’s cottage in the Lofoten Islands, Aronnax goes back over the notes he kept at sea. All three companions have reached land. What became of Nemo is the one thing the professor cannot put in his account.
